resolutions.researcher_notes: Egypt Oil & Gas feature (15 Jul 2024), citing Wood Mackenzie research, lists 'Korimat-Al Tebbin' among the 10 currently-existing main pipelines of the Nile Delta/Cairo/Nile Valley network, discussed in the present tense as part of the operating grid. Single source, medium tier.
Same article discusses Korimat-Al Tebbin as part of Egypt's natural gas transmission grid — a gas pipeline, not oil/NGL. Single source.

Korimat-Al Tebbin is listed among the 10 trunk lines making up the Nile Delta backbone of the national gas grid (alongside Abu Madi-Talkha, Talkha-Tanta-Cairo, Korimat-Beni Suef, etc.) — a transmission-grade interconnector between power-station supply points, not a local distribution line. Single source, medium tier.

The article gives only an aggregate capacity for all 10 Nile Delta lines combined (2,200 mmcf/d) and singles out Damanhur-Tanta specifically as the largest at 700.1 mmcf/d, implying the rest (including Korimat-Al Tebbin) are smaller — consistent with but not confirming the sheet's 110.00 MMcf/d. No per-line capacity figure found; checked the EGAS Annual Report 2018 (full pdftotext scan, no match) and GASCO's gas-grid page (no line-item list). No replacement found.

Article names the 'Korimat-Al Tebbin' pipeline (Korimat is the transliteration variant of Kuraimat used here), confirming a route between the Kuraimat power station and Al Tebbin — matching the sheet's StartLocation/EndPrefecture values. Note: the article does not itself state the governorates (Giza / Cairo), only the place names, so this supports the endpoint identification but not those specific governorate cells independently. Single source, medium tier.
